task_instance: Given a sample existing Now/Next/Later product roadmap and a user update request (add a new high-priority initiative 'SCIM provisioning' driven by enterprise deal risk, mark 'Bulk CSV export' as blocked/moved out of Now due to an external dependency, and identify what moves to make room), produce an updated roadmap summary following the skill's workflow: status overview, roadmap items grouped by Now/Next/Later with status/owner/target/dependencies, risks and dependencies section, changes-this-update summary, and a before/after comparison.
evidence: No project-management connector is available/allowed in this sandbox, so the skill's documented fallback path was used: 'ask the user to describe their current roadmap or paste/upload it' -> created current_roadmap.md as the sample input roadmap and update_request.txt as the sample user request (a new SCIM initiative plus a blocked dependency on Bulk CSV export). Produced the deliverable roadmap_update.md (72 lines, 4894 bytes) at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_gr/anthropics__knowledge-work-plugins__roadmap-update@developer-sandbox/roadmap_update.md, containing every section the SKILL.md workflow calls for: Status Overview, Roadmap Items (grouped Now/Next/Later with status/owner/target/dependencies table), Risks and Dependencies (including a contingency plan and a flagged capacity conflict), Changes This Update, a Before/After comparison table, and Recommended Follow-Ups (executive-summary offer, comms draft offer). Verified by listing the directory (ls -la) and grepping the markdown headings (grep -E '^#|^##' roadmap_update.md) to confirm all required sections are present, and by reviewing file contents for concrete, non-placeholder detail (specific owners, dates, dependency names, and a stated rationale for what got deprioritized to make room, per the skill's 'what comes off' rule). This is a pure reasoning/document-generation task with no dependency on any connector, script, or external service, so it was fully achievable within the developer sandbox using only file and shell tools.
